title: Plans and predictions
grammar: Will, Going to, Present Continuous for future
function: Talk about the future with different degrees of certainty

sections.heading: Three ways to talk about the future
sections.body: In English we use three main structures to talk about the future: 'will' for predictions and instant decisions, 'going to' for plans and intentions, and the Present Continuous for fixed arrangements.

sections.heading: Will
sections.body: Will + base verb. Used for predictions, promises, offers and instant decisions.
table: I think it will rain tomorrow.
I will help you with that.
I will have the soup, please.

sections.heading: Going to
sections.body: Am / is / are + going to + base verb. Used for plans and intentions, and for predictions based on evidence.
table: I am going to study medicine.
We are going to buy a house.

sections.heading: Present Continuous for future arrangements
sections.body: Used for fixed arrangements with a specific time and place.
list: I am meeting John at 7.
We are having dinner with friends tomorrow.
She is flying to Paris on Friday.

sections.heading: Time expressions for the future
list: tomorrow, the day after tomorrow
next week, next month, next year
this evening, tonight, this weekend
on Monday, in July, at 7 o'clock
soon, later, in a few days

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Do not say 'I will to go'. Say 'I will go'.
Do not forget 'to be' with going to: 'I going to' is wrong.
Do not confuse plans (going to) with predictions (will).

list.definition: I am going to travel to Italy next summer.
We are going to visit the museum.
She is going to study medicine.
They are going to buy a new car.
I am going to move to a new house.
He is going to start a new job.
We are going to learn French.
She is going to organise a party.
I am going to get a degree in engineering.
She is going to find a job abroad.
We are going to save money for a trip.
He is going to learn Japanese.
They are going to start a small business.
I am going to run a marathon next year.
I am going to buy a new smartphone.
She needs a new laptop for work.
He is going to get a tablet for his daughter.
I am going to download a new app.
They are going to design a website.
We are going to use social media more.
I think it will be sunny tomorrow.
I don't think she will come.
Maybe we will go to the beach.
I'm sure they will win.
He will probably be late.
I will definitely help you.

phases.name: Discovery
phases.intro: Look at these sentences. Read them carefully and think about the questions below.
sentences: I am going to visit my aunt next week.
She is going to study medicine.
They are not going to come to the party.
Are you going to travel this summer?
I am having lunch with my parents tomorrow.
I think it will rain tomorrow.
What are you doing this evening?
questions: In sentences 1 and 3, which structure do we use for plans and intentions?
In sentences 2 and 6, which tense do we use for fixed arrangements?
In sentence 4, how do we make a negative?
In sentence 5, how do we make a question?
In sentence 7, why do we use 'will' instead of 'going to'?

questions.prompt: I ___ visit my grandmother next Sunday.
questions.explanation: For plans we use am/is/are + going to + verb.

questions.prompt: She ___ study medicine next year.
We ___ buy a new house.
What ___ you ___ this evening?
questions.explanation: For arrangements we use Present Continuous.

questions.prompt: They ___ not going to come to the party.
questions.explanation: With 'they' the negative is 'are not going to'.

questions.prompt: I ___ meeting Sarah at 6.
questions.explanation: With 'I' we use 'am' in Present Continuous.

questions.prompt: I think it ___ rain tomorrow.
She ___ having lunch with her parents tomorrow.
___ you going to travel this summer?
We ___ going to learn French next year.

phases.name: Free practice
prompts: Write 5 sentences about your plans for next weekend. Use 'going to'.
Write 5 sentences about fixed arrangements you have this week. Use Present Continuous.
Write 3 predictions about the future using 'will'. Then write 3 plans using 'going to'.

questions.prompt: I ___ going to study tonight.
They ___ going to move to a new city.
She ___ playing tennis on Sunday.
questions.explanation: With 'she' we use 'is' in Present Continuous.

questions.prompt: We ___ going to visit Rome next spring.
What ___ you doing tomorrow?
questions.explanation: Present Continuous question: are + you + verb-ing.

questions.prompt: He ___ going to start a new job.
I think she ___ pass the exam.
They ___ having dinner at 8.
___ she going to come to the party?
I ___ going to learn to play the piano.

sections.heading: Key rules
list: Will + base verb: predictions, promises, offers, instant decisions.
Going to + base verb: plans, intentions, predictions with evidence.
Present Continuous: fixed future arrangements.
Negative: will not (won't), am/is/are + not + going to.
Question: Will + subject + verb? / Am/Is/Are + subject + going to...?

sections.heading: Common mistakes
list: Forgetting 'to be' with going to: 'I going to' is wrong.
Using 'going to' for instant decisions; use 'will'.
Confusing plans (going to) with arrangements (Present Continuous).

sections.heading: Useful phrases
list: I am going to...
We are going to...
I am meeting...
She is having lunch...
What are you doing...?
I think it will...
I will help you.
